ambiguities_or_notes: The same independently checked Greben Cossack vocabulary decisions as P004.06 are retained so the two variants remain directly comparable.
Канаусовый is rendered ‘kanaus-silk’ because канаус is a silk fabric; the culturally specific beshmet is retained rather than generalized to ‘coat.’

The official 90-volume electronic edition confirms the source's unusual line division ‘Вот уж видно, слава / Богу, Показалися значки.’ English therefore preserves the split as ‘thank / God’ rather than silently regularizing the verse.

Variant-specific readings are preserved: Ionka Grunin and Daddy Rodion replace the first variant's Vanka Grunin and Rodion Malashkin; ‘my sweetheart Kupriyan,’ the old sotnik's reply, movement of the cart toward them, and Kupriyashka's narrow belt are likewise kept distinct.
